messages:
maya: Heads-up — running a mixed-pool eviction game day tomorrow 09:00 PDT. Scope: edge regions (us-west-2 edge, eu-west-1 edge), mixed GPU pools (spot + reserved), and simulated network flaps between AZs. Goal: exercise automatic fallback routing + validate cost/capacity controls. Volunteers?

josh: I can lead the runbook. Can we verify which customer workloads are pinned to dedicated capacity first? don’t want accidental disruption.

maya: good call — SRE has the pinned list. @sre-bot please post pinned model routes for those regions.

sre-bot: Pinned routes exported: 
- customer-alpha: model-v3 (dedicated, us-west-2)
- finance-tenant: embeddings-prod (private, eu-west-1)
- sandbox: dev-model (hosted)

han: Suggest we run in two phases: 1) controlled node preemptions on non-pinned namespaces; 2) network partition emulation (packet loss + latency) to the edge proxy. Keep phase 1 below 30% of pool capacity.

priya: Also set cost guardrails — if fallback to reserved increases token-cost >15% vs baseline, abort and rollback. We should capture token latency and token cost delta.

zack: ops-bot can orchestrate the node drains and reattach failover routes. I'll queue a wasm job to do gradual evictions.

ops-bot: To simulate spot eviction use the following (dry-run first):
```
# mark node for eviction, cordon then drain
kubectl cordon gpu-spot-node-*
kubectl drain gpu-spot-node-1 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=30
# or simulate with node taint
kubectl taint nodes gpu-spot-node-1 preempt=true:NoSchedule
```

li: For network flaps I recommend tc qdisc on the edge proxy hosts: add 100-300ms delay and 5-10% packet loss for 60s windows. We can ramp up gradually.

eva: Success criteria proposal: 
- 99.9% of production requests for non-pinned customers served within SLA (p50/p95 target unchanged)
- No dropped persistent connections >1%
- Fallback path activated for >=95% of evicted requests (not returning 5xx)
- Cost delta on token spend <15% (per priya)
- Alerts triggered if tail latency >2x baseline for >5min

josh: Let's add an ops checklist: pre-game (snapshot metrics + create test org), run (execute phase 1 then phase 2), post-run (rollback taints, collect traces, perf report). Can someone make the perf snapshot job?

han: I'll push a Grafana snapshot and set a tracing span capture for the test window.

priya: Who's responsible for the canary traffic? We should shift 10% of synthetic traffic through the edge route to validate fallbacks before touching prod traffic.

maya: @zack you own canary traffic. Start with synthetic 10% for 30m, then proceed if stable.

zack: ack. I'll run synthetic canary using loadgen: 
```
loadgen --target https://edge-proxy.us-west-2.redwood-inference.internal --concurrency 50 --duration 30m --labels game-day-eviction
```

li: One more note — region quotas: eu-west-1 edge pool is at 82% reserved capacity. If we push evictions there, autoscaler may not add reserved nodes. Plan to pre-allocate +10% buffer or limit eviction rate in that region.

eva: Good catch. Let's cap eu-west-1 evictions at 10% of spot pool and pre-warm one reserved slab.

maya: Final roles: runbook lead @josh, canary + orchestration @zack, metrics & tracing @han, cost guard @priya, network sim @li, rollback lead @eva. Runbook link: https://internal.redwood/sec/infra/gameday-eviction (please review).

josh: I'm posting the condensed run order in this thread in 30m. If anyone sees blockers beforehand speak now.

priya: One blocker — billing team needs notice if we cross monthly reserved threshold for cost apportioning. I'll email them now.

maya: thanks team. Meeting invite sent 08:55 PDT so we can start the warmups at 09:00. :rocket:

zack: quick FYI — I'll record the run and upload logs to s3://redwood-gameday/1769993321/ after completion.

sre-bot: Reminder queued: create incident channel #gameday-1769993321 at 08:50 PDT.

li: 👍 prepping tc scripts and will lint the commands against the runbook.

josh: cool — if all good let's lock this. I'll put the step-by-step into the runbook and ping again.

maya: locking it. thanks everyone — rely on rapid rollback if anything violates the cost or SLA gates.
